userSymptom: Actual glyphs appear narrower and taller, like vertical stretching; confirmed explicitly by the user.

conditionalOldRendererMath.condition: A 402x778 layout drawn in 402x874 view bounds

sourceCauses: ReaderView full-bleed page/scroll children ignore safe areas, while the sole size observer measures the safe-area outer readerLayers. CoreTextPageViewController fills its real parent view bounds.
CoreTextPageView.renderPage stretches the entire page using independent width and height ratios. Hit testing, selection, annotations, attachment and live-media rects repeat that mapping.
CoreTextPageView uses the default resize content mode without a redraw-on-bounds policy, allowing a retained layer bitmap to stretch during resizing. Curl back images explicitly use scaleToFill.
correction: The existing size observer ignores the same safe areas as the actual reading surfaces; no second observer, viewport owner, or persistence path is added.

One centered uniform page transform drives drawing, inverse hit testing, selection/annotation/playback overlays, image taps, footnotes and inline live-media positions. Unoccupied destination bounds retain page background color.

CoreTextPageView redraws on bounds changes and preserves a pending bitmap aspect; curl back images preserve the same aspect. Existing engine snapshot/prefetch paths still use shared renderPage and their existing keys.
sourceAnalysis.fontReview: UserReaderFontResolver creates selected/system fonts at requested point size and applies weight/italic traits; reviewed regular font paths introduce no width/height scale. Global settings has no reader font aspect-scale migration. No user font data is inspected or changed.
preserved: CoreText pagination, fonts, font matrices and line metrics
Page bar and attachment positions within their sheet

findings.boundary: pointInRenderCoordinates, used by handleTap and attachment.linkTarget
findings.originalProblem: Attachment hit rectangles used the uniform page transform while the attachment-internal link lookup still inverted the old independent width and height scales. A visible table link or image footnote could therefore fail to activate at its painted location.
findings.arithmeticExample: For render 402x778 and view 402x874, the new sheet has scale 1 and y translation 48. A render point at y=74 paints at y=122. The previous inverse returned 122*778/874, approximately 108.60, rather than 74.
findings.existingRegressionBoundary: EPUBRenderingTests.tableFootnotePopoverAnchorsToMarkerNotWholeTable currently covers native-size real table-link taps; a changed-aspect variant would exercise this corrected branch.

findings.originalProblem: Live video and iframe views were still sent raw render-space attachment rectangles while their painted placeholders used the uniform page transform. The real inline view consequently appeared offset or incorrectly sized when page bounds and render size differed.
findings.verifiedCorrection: currentLiveAttachments now maps attachment.rect through pageView.viewRect(forRenderRect:) and converts that page-view rectangle into the controller view coordinates consumed by InlineLiveViewHost. Both initial embedding and layout reconciliation use that same function.
findings.existingRegressionBoundary: InlineLiveViewHostTests.webEmbedLifecycle covers host reconciliation but does not itself cover the page controller's attachment mapping. The new resizedLivePageRedrawsWithoutStretching definition covers the page bitmap, not a real live media child.

acceptedSourceFacts: The uniform PageGeometry is reused by compositor drawing, text inverse hits, attachment internal inverse hits, image hit rectangles, selection, annotation layers, note marker anchors and TTS selection rectangles.

Bounds changes already recalculate annotation, playback and selection overlays; contentMode redraw now requests a new page bitmap, while contentsGravity preserves the preceding bitmap aspect until it is replaced.
Live-media child coordinates now include the same presentation transform and page-view to owner-view conversion.
The proportional curl-back image contract is explicitly asserted in its existing fixture.
ReaderView adds ignoresSafeArea only to the measurement observer, matching the existing full-bleed reader children. Its single modifier hunk must be composed with the callback ReaderView work.
No definite newly introduced Swift API, signature or fixture compilation blocker was identified from the inspected source.

notes: Source acceptance is conditional on the exact v2 hashes and does not claim an Apple SDK build or passing tests.
The two source findings were communicated before the author corrected them; the reviewer did not edit candidate source.
Root must bind the final callback-plus-glyph ReaderView composition and run the focused synthetic pixel, viewport, curl-back and writing-mode regressions on the Apple SDK.

sharedReaderViewComposition.method: Compose exactly one observer modifier hunk over callback implementation, preserving all callback changes.

newDefinitions.purpose: Actual synthetic CJK/Latin horizontal and vertical CoreText crop pixels, selection dimensions, point hit and attachment mapping preserve aspect for 402x778 to 402x874.
Portrait/landscape/half-size/nonzero-origin sheet mappings preserve square aspect and round-trip the inverse.
Real CoreTextPageView.layer display replaces the bitmap after actual bounds change, with unchanged glyph crop pixels.
Two actual UIKit-backed SwiftUI observer callbacks report equal full-bleed child/probe sizes despite added safe-area insets.
